76830ec3aedc: Ask: «Co robiliście w weekend? Co zrobiliście?» Write two columns on the board and don't explain the difference — let the students work it out themselves.
24eefdc1aa39: Same idea as English «was making» vs «made»: process versus result. In Polish the two meanings are two different verbs.
e5f1aec55cb9: English has no aspect pairs, so the prefix has to be learned together with the verb: pisać — napisać, robić — zrobić. Ask for 3 pairs the student already knows and have them translated.
1e49e15b439c: There is no rule for which prefix goes with which verb. Learn them in pairs, like English phrasal verbs (give up, give in).
7393dbabb497: Hint: the longer form is the imperfective one (kupować, dawać); the shorter one is perfective (kupić, dać).
1afd5a723a9e: Most important: «zrobię» is already the future tense, like English «I will do». «Będę zrobić» does not exist.
384cb529823d: These pairs are not formed with a prefix — they are different stems, as in English go — went. Trap: “said” ≠ skazał.
47d7ec6c575e: Ask the student to find 3 signal words in the text of lesson 3, and the verbs next to them.
b5e7d3c9decb: While I was sculpting, the phone rang.
d97c2dc15ba5: I finished the bowl and left.
d291daa452f7: I was listening to music and sculpting.
362d806652c3: Draw a long line (background) and a short arrow (action) on the board. Students make up their own sentences with kiedy.
01de1884fa8e: English has no aspect here (he started playing), so the rule is new: zacząć grać, never «zacząć zagrać». Students make this mistake with Polish verbs very often.
79baa24057d5: I learned to mould things in a month.
e80c09df54c2: English «in a month» covers both: «within a month» = w miesiąc, and «a month from now» = za miesiąc. That is the trap in s17.
e5e91bca1b4e: Right now I'm making a mug.
8ee8b76ee5cf: Tomorrow I will make a mug.
454fce09b47f: What will you do on the weekend?
045d2cc34fba: English has no perfective, so a form that looks like the present («zrobię») always meaning the future is new. Ask three students to say what they will do today after the lesson.
dd0048fd04a8: I learned it in a year
a2d725f509c5: The second three are lexical false friends. The funny «skazał» especially — students remember it.
